summary.intent: Push a completed Phase 21 branch to GitHub and resolve all open PR review comments from automated reviewers.
summary.outcome: Branch divergence with origin was reconciled, the push succeeded, and all 5 Copilot review threads on PR #346 were triaged and resolved (4 fixed, 1 already addressed).

repo: Project uses a .planning/ directory with per-phase subdirectories (e.g., .planning/phases/21-byo-ipfs-node-support/) containing VALIDATION.md and UI-SPEC.md files.
ROADMAP.md tracks phase status and required manual update from 'Not started' to 'complete' for Phase 21.
GitHub repo is FSM1/cipher-box; branch naming convention is docs/phase-NN-description.

code.finding: Had multiple issues flagged by Copilot requiring fixes — 3 separate edits needed.
Had one Copilot comment requiring a fix.
Phase 21 status conflicted between local (complete) and remote (Not started) due to GitHub web UI merge; local version was correct.

workflow: Merging via GitHub web UI creates a remote commit that local branch doesn't have, causing divergence that must be reconciled with a local merge before pushing.
When resolving divergence where both sides merged the same upstream, merge conflicts are minimal but ROADMAP.md status fields are a common conflict point.
PR review thread resolution requires both a REST reply (with integer comment ID via --field) and a GraphQL mutation to mark resolved — two separate API calls per thread.

friction: Branch diverged from origin because a merge conflict was resolved via GitHub web UI, requiring an extra local merge step before pushing.
ROADMAP.md merge conflict had to be manually resolved — remote had stale 'Not started' status while local had the correct 'complete' status.
open_items: git push was executed but the transcript does not confirm thread replies and GraphQL resolve mutations completed — thread resolution replies may still be pending.
No test run (typecheck/unit/e2e) was recorded after the PR review edits to planning docs — likely skipped since changes were documentation-only, but worth confirming policy.
